method: Built-in image generation; model version not exposed

outputs.title: Clothing and player silhouette
outputs.observation: White draped hooded garment; geometric orange/black/turquoise poncho; striped cream/red/green/blue serape.
outputs.proposal: Candidate costume mass, hem motion and palette. The campus hoodie is discussed but not photographed. Choose one base silhouette before making animation.
outputs.limitations: Generated mannequin wear and close-up fabric views are reconstructed, not photographed turnaround evidence.

outputs.title: Chair · grip and action
outputs.hook: An ordinary chair, an unreasonable solution
outputs.observation: Curved honey plywood seat/back, black metal legs; horizontal hold, overhead preparation, lowered follow-through and guard-like orientations.
outputs.proposal: Chair-first melee is proposed in A12. Prototype one strike with readable anticipation/contact/recovery; up/down/horizontal variants and block are owner-requested pose studies, not a completed moveset.
outputs.limitations: Mannequins replace the photographed people. These are static pose endpoints; grips, joint motion, exact leg attachment and in-between frames need review at game scale.

outputs.title: Tray · hold and guard
outputs.observation: Mustard-yellow shallow rectangular tray, rounded corners and raised lip; stack, face, edge and demonstrated horizontal/vertical holds.
outputs.proposal: A12 proposes a later returning throw for kiting. Owner also requests attack/block studies. The photos establish holds/guard, not an airborne tray path or full attack cycle.
outputs.limitations: People become neutral mannequins. Throw, catch, down/up attacks and collision timing remain future original animation work.

outputs.title: Robots · potential enemies
outputs.observation: Exposed six-legged walker, four yellow-wheel sensor rover and open-frame quadrotor, with wiring and joint detail.
outputs.proposal: Original enemy silhouettes can borrow mechanical vocabulary: grounded rover first, walker later, hard-to-kill drone as avoidance pressure. The earlier cute campus robot remains an optional collectible, not automatically hostile.
outputs.limitations: Glass glare and cabinet clutter removed. Scale mannequins, reconstructed parts and detail crops are interpretive; no measured scale or verified joint rig. Do not copy the university projects as shipped designs.

outputs.title: Mensa food · pickups and boss shapes
outputs.hook: Lunch can wait. Or can it?
outputs.observation: Muffin with pale center; dark/light layered cake; chocolate-coated wafer; round Leberkaese roll in paper.
outputs.proposal: Owner requests potential food-boss material. Optional original encounter seed: The Lunch Rush, a roll that winds up, rolls across a lane and pauses exposed. This is a new design suggestion, not a recorded team choice. Food pickups and defense jokes remain alternatives.
outputs.limitations: No monster is fabricated inside the food reference board. Mannequin scale and reconstructed food surfaces are illustrative, not measurements. Boss silhouette, tells, hit region and budget are still open.

outputs.title: Drinks and refreshment props
outputs.observation: Brown coffee cup/carton; strawberry milk bottle; green-cap iced tea; twin-hopper coffee machine; white mugs.
outputs.proposal: Possible pickup vocabulary or station prop. Choose at most one simple effect after the core loop works; no separate consumables/economy system is implied.
outputs.limitations: Brand lettering is removed or abstracted. Held-product inserts and unseen packaging details are generated interpretation; drinks are not assigned health/speed values.

outputs.title: Technology and future upgrades
outputs.hook: An experiment that fits in a suitcase
outputs.observation: Open silver experiment case with black lid screen and exposed board/terminals; green student racing-car poster motifs.
outputs.proposal: Case/map-information upgrade is discussed; transformation into a building is an unselected idea. Race-car imagery is future mechanical inspiration, not a promised vehicle or weapon.
outputs.limitations: Case controls are reconstructed. Race-car views are inferred from poster pictures, not direct vehicle photographs; team faces/history are replaced by abstract graphics. Not a measured engineering model.

outputs.title: Wayfinding and future pole props
outputs.observation: Slender galvanized post, two yellow outlined panels, upward arrows and green assembly-point pictogram beside campus buildings.
outputs.proposal: Possible later pole-weapon or navigation joke. Preserve the shape/material reference without adopting the original slogan or the off-topic jokes as game dialogue.
outputs.limitations: Original wording is replaced with neutral arrows/glyphs; people become a mannequin or are removed. This is design interpretation, not a documentary image of campus signage or evidence of a weapon demonstration.

rights: Owner-supplied reference photography. Third-party designs/marks retain their rights; no automatic runtime license.
review: All source contact sheets and finished boards visually inspected. Generated views/details/scales remain interpretations; team approval pending.
